paragraphs.text: # idsh
> Dockerized DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) web UI.
## Packages
| Package                                          | Description
| Version
| `@idsh/mobile`               | Touch CSS, Enter as a line break, and the home-screen icon

| [](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@idsh/mobile)               |
| `@idsh/privileged-ui`
| The settings page over a non-loopback origin, delegating the decision to dsh  | [](https://www.npm

js.com/package/@idsh/privileged-ui) |
| `@idsh/remote-access` | Keeps the UI's multiplexed WebSocket
alive across a stalled connection        | [](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@idsh/remote-access) |
| `@idsh/host-broker`     | The host side of `@idsh/host-ops`: a typed, audited socket (not a dsh pl

ugin) | [](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@idsh/host-broker)     |
| `@idsh/host-ops`           | The
dsh tools that ask the host broker over a unix socket                     | [](https://www.npmjs.co
m/package/@idsh/host-ops)           |
## Documentation

The plan for the next version is in `ROADMAP.md`: reaching the host, the LAN and
the router, and dep

loying through the same channel. Phase 1 has started:
`@idsh/host-broker` is the host side, and
`@id
sh/host-ops` turns that table into dsh tools.

`pnpm docs:dev` serves this README, `ROADMAP.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, each package's `README.md` and
`CH

ANGELOG.md`, and the image's changelog; `pnpm docs:build` writes a static copy to `dist/`. The
Markd
own files are the source — there is nothing to keep in sync.
## Requirements

- Docker with BuildKit and Docker Compose **2.24.4+** (the channel overlays use `!reset`), plus
Node
.js **≥24** and pnpm **12.16.1** — the pins in `package.json` — with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

`
run once in the checkout.
## Getting started

1. Provide the host uid/gid (export them, or drop them in a `.env`
in this directory):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`.env` is gitignored, so it is safe to keep in the working directory.

The DeepSeek API key is **not** an environment variable: add it once the container is up, in the
web

UI's settings. It is kept in the state directory, so it survives a rebuild and never reaches
the im
age or the process environment.
2. Create your compose file from the template and start the development channel.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

That is the development channel. Without the broker checkout, `Dockerfile.dev` takes its client
from

a published image instead (`--build-arg GCB_CLIENT_IMAGE=ghcr.io/code-vaults/gcb-client:<tag>`),
an

d `GCB_IMAGE` can name a published broker; its config/key still come from `~/.broker-host`.
A long-l

ived deployment does not build at all: it runs the pinned images from
`docker-compose.prod.yml` — se
e `pnpm deploy:prod` below.

The copy is the base; `docker-compose.broker.yml` defines the credential broker
(its config, key and

`user.refresh` come from `~/.broker-host`, see the broker's
own README). **A fresh checkout without

that directory** can still deploy: run
`gcb init`/`gcb authorize` there once, or drop the broker fi

le and supervise the
broker on the host — the file's own header says how. The channel overlay picks

ker in
its container is the recommended shape** — one definition, one lifecycle with the
deployment,

and the socket shared through the state directory. A host-supervised
broker is still supported: dro

p the broker file — and with it the IPv6 network
settings it carries — **bind-mount its socket direc

tory into the container** (the
template already mounts the state directory, `./.dsh:/home/app/.dsh`,

so a socket
under `.dsh/git-broker` needs no extra volume) and set `GIT_BROKER_SOCKET` to the
path

**inside the container** (`/home/app/.dsh/git-broker/broker.sock`), not the
host's. `entrypoint.sh`
runs `gcb setup` only when that path exists.
[该节后续省略]
## Configuration
Environment variables (see `docker-compose.example.yml`):
| Variable                                                | Purpose
| Default                           |
| `PUID` / `PGID`                                         | uid/gid dsh runs as (and owns bind-mount
ed files as); compose forwards the host's `$UID`/`$GID`
| `$UID` / `$GID`                   |
| `NPM_REGISTRY`                                          | npm/pnpm/yarn registry: the image build
and the user-level configs use it (the release build on GitHub Actions passes the official one)
| `https://registry.npmmirror.com/`

|
| `DSH_TRUSTED_HOSTS`                                     | Space-separated host authorities allow
ed by dsh's browser-trust fence

|
| `DSH_PUBLIC_URL`                                        | Public HTTP(S) root to advertise behi
nd a prefix-stripping proxy; pair it with `DSH_TRUSTED_HOSTS`

|
| `DSH_BIND_HOST`                                         | Concrete address dsh binds, defaulti
ng to the container's own (the wildcard is refused): set it to `127.0.0.1` to give up remote reach,
or to one address when several networks make the default ambiguous | this container

ress when several networks make the default ambiguous | this container                    |
[该节后续省略]
### What it does not do

- It is **not a sandbox**: a repository the allowlist admits is one the agent can push to, and the
A

pp's permissions bound what a push can change. That is the intended boundary, not a gap.
- It does *

*not** keep a credential for anything else — it is not a secret store, and it does not
cover registr

ies, npm tokens or ssh.
- It changes **nothing** when the socket is not mounted: `entrypoint.sh` ski

ps the setup, no helper
is configured, and the deployment behaves exactly as before.
